hook: Graphene's electrons flow like a fluid, and a new device measures their viscosity directly.
hook_turn: and a new device measures their viscosity directly.
summary: Corbino-shaped graphene devices let magnetoresistance separate ohmic resistance from viscous flow in the same sample. In monolayer and bilayer graphene the electron-electron scattering rate rises linearly with temperature, not as T squared as in ordinary metals, matching a predicted tomographic fluid regime. The match to theory is consistent with, not proof of, that regime, and only graphene was tested.
title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids.
